I'll say that the springing motion when nodes finally spill out of their bubble can be pretty harsh, but I will admit that it settles quite nicely. 

Back on the 2D Local Map, I'm seeing overall improvements. I'll admit that my hope for the act of zooming in and out to be simple was uh, quite overambitious! I am at that point where I'm going... "soooo maybe like very very FEW breakpoints (2-3) for heavily quanitized different looks of the nodes and we _don't_ try to scale fonts automatically during zoom-out? I need the eye of a designer on the particular mechanics of zooming in and out in the 2D Local map. All I know is how it feels when I operate it, and it feels... clunky? It feels a little uglier than it was, say, a month ago before I started the escapades to make certain things zoom-invariant inside it and display the contents that were previously relegated to the Detail Panel over on the actual node cards. I wish I had better and more design language in my hands so I could better describe what feels off, but my best guess is that I am simply seeing too much unexpected change as I zoom. I feel like if we're going to have to have visual changes to ensure a reasonable readable layout at far zooms, then perhaps those changes should just be quantized and sufficiently few in number so as to not be jarring on _every_ zoom interaction. 

What I will say is that the first pass you've completed has resolved a fair few of the countless nits, and part of me wonders if it's wiser for me to let you simply continue to judge and iterate and dispatch builders to remediate. 

Last item: 345 out of 350 browser tests... why are we failing? Are these flaky timing fails due to absence of sufficient computing horsepower at the time of the test execution?
